content_record.title: Urolithin A restores calcium-driven organelle crosstalk to trigger mitophagy and slow ageing
content_record.editorial_body: A gut metabolite reopens ER–mitochondria–lysosome communication via calcium sparks, reviving mitochondrial quality control and extending healthspan in worms and human cells. Three things to remember - UA releases ER calcium, driving DRP-1 fission and mitophagy. - Calcium chelation blocks UA's benefits on muscle and lifespan. - UA boosts mitochondrial biogenesis via CAMK2D and Nrf2. Source This signal is based on Urolithin Α modulates inter-organellar communication via calcium-dependent mitophagy to promote healthy ageing. from PubMed. Read the original report for full context. Health note: Preclinical evidence only; human trials needed to confirm dosage and safety.
